title: Catch in the right order
description:
Write `std::string outcome(const std::function<void()>& action)`. It runs `action` and reports what happened:

| What `action` does | Return |
|---|---|
| finishes normally | `"ok"` |
| throws `std::out_of_range` | `"out of range: "` + the message |
| throws any other `std::logic_error` | `"logic error: "` + the message |
| throws any other `std::exception` | `"error: "` + the message |
| throws something that is not a `std::exception` | `"unknown"` |

`std::out_of_range` **is a** `std::logic_error`, which **is a** `std::exception`. Catch blocks are tried from top to bottom and the first match wins, so the most specific type must come first. Catch by `const&`.

Then write `std::string retried(const std::function<void()>& action, int attempts)`: it calls `action` up to `attempts` times, stopping at the first call that does not throw, and returns `"ok after N"` (N = how many calls it took) or `"gave up"`.
hints: Put the `catch` blocks from the most specific to the most general: `std::out_of_range`, then `std::logic_error`, then `std::exception`, then `catch (...)`. A general one placed first would catch everything.
Catch by `const&` and use `e.what()` for the message.
